trigger.symptom: Both tasks of the original stage3-wide-latent launch (Beaker exp 01M22Q2AF2JNNJP69RWQ8CG4AA, latent_size=256, batch_size=1024, 2 seeds) failed after ~53 min at JIT-compile time with 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Out of memory while trying to allocate 1513245575640 bytes' (~1.38 TiB requested vs 141GB available on the H200). hlo_rematerialization.cc:3022 logged: "Can't reduce memory use below 99.55GiB (106890456652 bytes) by rematerialization; only reduced to 1.38TiB (1513264486324 bytes), down from 1.38TiB (1513264510944 bytes) originally" -- i.e. XLA's own rematerialization pass could barely touch it.
trigger.cause: HkDisentangledRNN.update_latents (disentangled_rnns/library/disrnn.py) builds ONE separate ResMLP per latent in a Python-level `for net_i in range(latent_size)` loop, unrolled at JAX trace time rather than vmapped. At latent_size=256 (vs. 5 in all prior studies) this is a ~51x increase in the number of update-net modules traced into one XLA graph. A follow-up batch_size=64 smoke test (n_steps=50, same latent_size=256, one-off exp 01M23R8FKZSW7D1CDQZFSNDGW4) confirmed this is NOT primarily a batch-size-scaled activation-memory problem: it did not reproduce the RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED OOM, but instead hit a different, batch-size-independent failure at the same training-step JIT-compile point: 'INVALID_ARGUMENT: Can't pack device memory arguments array of size 1793 which is larger than the maximum supported size of 1024' -- a fixed PJRT argument-packing ceiling driven by the number of separate per-latent module parameter buffers (~7 packed args/latent x 256 = 1793), independent of batch size. Root cause: the per-latent loop's graph/argument-count term dominates, not activation memory, so no batch_size cut can fix latent_size=256 -- it needs `update_latents` to `vmap` its per-latent loop instead of Python-unrolling it (wrapper code fix, tracked in a GitHub issue on aind-dynamic-foraging-bfm-wrapper).

deviations.reason_for_config_change: latent_size=256 (the original GRU-H256-matched ceiling-probe target) is infeasible on current hardware/wrapper code (see trigger.cause). Downgraded to latent_size=32 per explicit user steering rather than continuing to chase 256 via batch-size tricks. This makes stage3-wide-latent a REDUCED ceiling probe, not the study's original GRU-parity target; true latent_size=256 remains blocked on a wrapper vmap fix.
deviations.sizing_probes_budget_note: Per steering: at most ~2-3 total sizing probes. Used: (1) batch_size=64 smoke test at latent_size=256 [confirmed batch-size-independent failure, did not retry batch_size=16 since the error was unambiguously a fixed argument-count ceiling, not a size-scaled one], (2) latent_size=32 sizing probe at standard batch_size=1024 [passed]. A first smoke-test submission (01M23R4PMW6C88W4JQM7A1BSEG) failed immediately on a config-key error (batch_size lives under `data.batch_size`, not `model.training.batch_size`) and is not counted as a real sizing probe.

cost.note: Both original tasks OOM'd before any checkpoint was written; zero progress discarded.
